o1.biggest_strength: It nails the diagnosis and the guardrail: a flat 15-channel plan aimed squarely at Essentials 8+ churners, with a stop rule that hinges on the one number that actually matters — how many Team 8+ users downgrade.
o1.biggest_mistake: The revenue math is shaky: it claims $247,400 is wrong ($257,400), its blended per-customer revenue figures don't reconcile, and the mid-case +$57k over six months vs +$17.5k at month 6 exposes a math error that would make me distrust the whole table.
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: Rebuild the revenue model from the ground up so every number reconciles, then add the churn-reduction savings explicitly rather than through a per-customer arithmetic that doesn't tie out.

o2.biggest_strength: The customer email in the brand voice — showing the customer their own current bill beside the new price, no deadlines, a switch-back promise — is exactly how Buffer should talk, and there's a clean customer-facing angle plus a clear break-even number (1 in 3 Team downgrades).
o2.biggest_mistake: The downside case is under-stressed: it says net -$20.3k/month at month 6 but doesn't show what makes the board call it off within two quarters, and the 2-user limit isn't fully reconciled with the 15-channel freelance use case.
o2.what_would_make_it_a_10: Tie the Agency per-channel ceiling to a real definition of the freelance use case (e.g. number of clients not channels) and add a month-by-month cash view so the board sees exactly when it turns positive.

reason: Both pick the right plan, but Output 2's math holds together better and its customer email is genuinely in our voice, whereas Output 1's numbers don't reconcile and would have me re-checking every figure before trusting the recommendation.
